content.title: About
content.content: Buckwheat, whole grain is the intact seed of the buckwheat plant (Fagopyrum esculentum), cultivated in temperate regions of Europe and Asia. It has a nutty, slightly earthy flavor and a firm texture. Buckwheat is eaten boiled as a cereal, ground into flour, or added to salads and soups.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Buckwheat is not a true cereal grain but a pseudocereal, like quinoa.
Its seeds are rich in rutin, a flavonoid that strengthens capillary walls.
Buckwheat has long been considered a “superfood” in Russian and Ukrainian cuisine.
In Japan buckwheat is used to make soba noodles, which can be 100 % buckwheat or blended with wheat.
Buckwheat can grow on poor, rocky soils where many other crops fail.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Buckwheat provides about 13 % protein, including all essential amino acids, making it a valuable plant‑based protein source.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Consuming whole‑grain buckwheat helps maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and benefits gut health.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Buckwheat supplies magnesium, iron, zinc, and manganese, which are important for nerve and muscle function.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Flavonoids such as rutin and quercetin protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to buckwheat.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Buckwheat contains oxalates, so individuals prone to kidney stones should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Cross‑contamination
items.content: Although buckwheat is gluten‑free, processing on equipment that also handles wheat can lead to cross‑contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Buckwheat can be boiled as a porridge, added to salads, soups, and casseroles, or milled into flour for gluten‑free breads and pancakes. Rinsing and soaking the grains for about 30 minutes before cooking shortens the cooking time.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store whole‑grain buckwheat in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent the fats from becoming rancid.
